page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core), backed by 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It comes equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, and includes a 644 GB local SSD for temporary scratch space.

Benchmark evaluations place the D16ds_v4 consistently in the middle tiers across compute and memory operations. It recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 1201.0 and a multi-core score of 7231.0, paired with a multi-core stress-ng rating of 14891.9. In memory throughput, the architecture delivers 79.84 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 45.97 GB/sec for uncached write operations, while cached small-block reads achieve 831.03 GB/sec. Instruction support covers AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, helping PassMark extended instructions reach 14414.55 points.

Workload testing highlights solid throughput for caching, database, and web infrastructure. The instance executes 14.01 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 12.0 GB/sec of static web serving throughput, while PassMark database operations benchmark at 5724.25. Without a dedicated GPU, LLM inference on medium 7B models demonstrates weak prompt processing at 24.63 tokens/sec. Consequently, the configuration is best matched to relational databases, in-memory caches, application backends, CI/CD build workers, and web server tiers requiring local scratch SSD storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per vCPU), and a local 644 GB SSD. It features hardware extensions including AVX-512 and AES cryptography. Across synthetic tests, the instance registers average-tier performance, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 7231.0, 14.01 million Redis SET operations per second, and 12.0 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Compute-only model execution remains limited for large machine learning tasks due to the lack of hardware accelerators. With balanced compute and memory capacity combined with high-speed local disk storage, the D16ds_v4 serves effectively as an enterprise application server, relational or caching database host, software compilation node, or container host.
